sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash — Gemini API model documentation
sources.evidence: Names stable gemini-2.5-flash; lists 1,048,576 input tokens, 65,536 output tokens, text/image/video/audio inputs, text output, thinking and function calling. The page says existing users retain API access and does not disclose parameter counts. This documents specifications, not a tested live endpoint.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes
sources.evidence: June 17, 2025 explicitly releases gemini-2.5-flash as the first stable 2.5 Flash. Separate entries release gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04-17 on April 17 and gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20 on May 20.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5: Pushing the Frontier with Advanced Reasoning, Multimodality, Long Context, and Next Generation Agentic Capabilities
sources.evidence: Reopened on October 27. Table 1 has an exact Gemini 2.5 Flash column for modalities, context, thinking and tools. Section 2.1 describes sparse MoE Transformers and says smaller models, Flash size and below, use distillation; it does not identify a known-size base whose nominal count can be inherited. No numerical total, active count or expert routing ratio is disclosed. The 22-billion and trillion-parameter references are other research, not this model. Audio output is experimental/preview rather than the stable text endpoint.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash and native capabilities — Model Card, December 2025
sources.evidence: Reopened on October 27. The current PDF says December 2025, although the model-card index labels its link September 26. It identifies sparse MoE Transformer architecture and distinguishes Flash text from Image and Audio outputs. Routing is qualitative: no total, active, expert count or numeric activation fraction. The card spans several versions; exact endpoint limits remain grounded in s1.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash — Google Cloud model documentation
sources.evidence: Names gemini-2.5-flash, documents a 1,048,576-token context, thinking/function calling, text output, image/audio/video input, and application/pdf document input. The page also states retirement on October 20, 2026, so it is retained as specification evidence and not proof of current Cloud endpoint availability.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5: Updates to our family of thinking models
sources.evidence: June 17, 2025 announcement confirms stable/general availability for Gemini 2.5 Flash and explicitly states no changes from the May 20 preview. Calls Flash a model series and describes controllable thinking.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Governs access to Gemini API and AI Studio through service terms and prohibits extracting or replicating underlying models, including parameter weights. Together with the exact-model hosted API documentation, supports closed-weight/proprietary classification; documentation and sample-code licenses do not license the model weights.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Flash — Model Card, December 2025
sources.evidence: Rechecked the December 2025 card on October 27. Its exact Gemini 3 Flash versus Gemini 2.5 Flash table reports safety, tone and unjustified-refusal changes; it has no total or activated-parameter column. No sibling size is transferred.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash — Model Card, September 2026
sources.evidence: Rechecked the September 2026 card and comparison table on October 27. Its documented base is Gemini 3.7 Flash, not Gemini 2.5 Flash; it gives no retrospective total or active count for the older model.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon — Model Card, October 2026
sources.evidence: Rechecked the October 2026 card on October 27. It describes Argon as a new model rather than a modification or fine-tune of a prior model, and gives no numerical parameter disclosure for Gemini 2.5 Flash. The older model cannot inherit Argon specifications.

sources.title: Thinking to recall: How reasoning unlocks parametric knowledge in LLMs
sources.evidence: June 24, 2026 research studies Gemini 2.5 Flash reasoning via controlled trace replacement and factual priming. It provides no numerical production parameter disclosure; its parametric-knowledge discussion is not a parameter-count claim. Architecture is established directly by s3 and s4.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 2.5 Flash catalog record
sources.evidence: Followed the baseline source URL as a catalog lead. Technical and release assertions in this audit are grounded in Google's own documentation and reports instead.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash pricing and specifications
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model searches surfaced an 18B total claim. Opened on October 27: the page states 18B but supplies no developer citation attached to that specification. Its source list describes pricing provenance, and its disclaimer identifies third-party aggregation. This is an unresolved numerical lead, not accepted parameter evidence.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report, October 2026
sources.evidence: Inspected full text from the October 27 HTTP 200 PDF download; the web reader rejected the file size. Section 6.1.3, printed page 211, retrospectively calls Gemini 2.5 Flash smaller than 2.5 Pro while comparing prompt-injection robustness. This is a qualitative comparison with no total or active size. Other parameter occurrences concern task difficulty, security or parametric knowledge, not numerical model size.

sources.title: Thinking to Recall: How Reasoning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs
sources.publisher: Gekhman et al.; linked by Google Research
sources.evidence: Followed the paper from Google Research on October 27. Section 2 studies Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro alongside Qwen3-32B; Appendix A.2 reports inference settings rather than weight counts. No total or active count for Gemini 2.5 Flash appears, and the Qwen size is not a Gemini specification.

name.note: Official display name for the stable gemini-2.5-flash identifier.

developer.note: The report is authored by Gemini Team, Google; the release announcement is by Google DeepMind product staff.

family.note: Catalog normalization of Google's Gemini Flash model series, retained as the existing family key.

release_date.note: Earliest public release of the exact underlying model: May20 preview. Google explicitly says the June17 stable release has no changes from that preview. April17 was an earlier distinct revision; June17 is stable-ID availability.

open_weights.note: Distributed as a hosted Gemini API model under terms restricting extraction of underlying weights; no open-weight distribution is offered for this endpoint.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the closed hosted model under Gemini service terms, not an SPDX license or the documentation page's CC-BY/sample-code license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-model total-size and named-base searches, reopened original evidence, and later Google comparisons found no supported nominal total. The report explicitly describes distillation for Flash-size models, not a count-preserving relationship to a named known-size base. SuperBased's 18B claim has no linked developer support. The report's 22B vision-transformer reference and later paper's Qwen3-32B are different models. Total remains null rather than inheriting a teacher or sibling size.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 searches for active and activated parameters, full-text checks of the original report/card, and later Google comparisons found no numerical active count. Sparse routing is documented, but expert count and activation fraction are not. The 3 Flash comparison is safety/tone, the Argon report supplies only a qualitative smaller-model comparison, and the research paper gives inference settings. No active value is inferred from total size, token limits, a teacher or a sibling.

architecture.note: Sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer with native multimodal inputs, explicitly described in technical-report section 2.1 and the exact Flash model card. The catalog's moe key captures the disclosed architecture.

context_window.note: Exact input/context token limit for gemini-2.5-flash. Its separate maximum output is 65,536 tokens.

modalities.note: Exact endpoint supports text/image/audio/video input and text output; Google Cloud explicitly lists application/pdf input. Image and native-audio output belong to separately identified variants and are not inherited.

reasoning.note: Thinking is supported with a configurable budget and can be disabled; the boolean denotes capability rather than mandatory use on every request.

tool_call.note: The exact endpoint's capability table explicitly supports function calling.

description.value: Multimodal Gemini model with configurable thinking, a 1,048,576-token context window, and function calling.
description.note: Replaces qualitative workhorse/latency/price wording with directly documented capabilities.

patch.description: Multimodal Gemini model with configurable thinking, a 1,048,576-token context window, and function calling.

sources.label: Gemini 2.5: Updates to our family of thinking models

patch.notes: Sparse MoE Transformer; Google does not disclose total or active parameter counts in the reviewed sources. First released as the May 20, 2025 preview; Google explicitly states the June 17 stable release uses the same model. The April 17 preview was an earlier revision.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: total and active counts remain undisclosed after fresh exact-model searches, original report/card checks, later Google comparisons and a named-base review. Investigated an unsupported third-party 18B claim and distinguished distillation from count-preserving lineage. Explicit null patches added. All unrelated audited fields and corrections retained.
